title: OpenAI Responses compatibility ledger and graceful degradation strategy
creator: Sophie Caldwell
description: Produce a canonical compatibility ledger that maps Redwood Responses behavior to the OpenAI Responses API semantics, surface graded parity gaps (behavioral, streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs), and define deterministic runtime fallback/degradation strategies. Deliverables: 1) compatibility ledger artifact (CSV/markdown) with operators and edge cases; 2) a fallback playbook for runtime routing and user-visible errors; 3) a test matrix and CI gating spec for parity-sensitive regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger created containing mapping for message events, streaming event types, function calling handshake, tool-call argument shapes, and structured output annotations
Gap classification present for each entry (behavioral-lossy | behavioral-preserved | protocol-delta | unsupported) with example repros
Fallback playbook defines deterministic routing: preferred model variant -> graceful degrade to compatible variant -> synthetic partial response -> structured error payload
CI tests (unit + integration) added to runtime repo that assert key parity behaviors and fail on regressions
Runbook and example dashboard query included in the Console to surface parity regressions by model, route, and customer tier
blocking_issues: Missing schema for structured-output annotations in runtime (blocked canonicalization)
End-to-end streaming harness instability on ARM-nightly machines
comments: 2025-02-15 Sophie Caldwell: Kickoff meeting notes: aligned on scope — focus on behavioral deltas around streaming event ordering, partial tool-call payloads, and structured output lossiness. Decided ledger should be human-readable and machine-parsable (CSV + JSONL).

2025-02-18 Markus Li: Initial inventory script added to runtime repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2789). Script extracts event types emitted by our streaming stack and normalizes names to OpenAI spec tokens. Observed 6 unmatched event types so far.

2025-02-22 Anika Bose (PM): Prioritized parity gaps impacting customers: (1) streamed function call mid-event vs final function call, (2) structured-object validation failures for partial outputs, (3) streaming-of-tool-progress events. Marked these as highest priority for mitigation.

2025-02-27 Markus Li: PoC fallback behavior implemented in local dev branch: if streaming event contains unknown-type, runtime emits structured-error with 'compat_issue' code and falls back to poll-for-final-result. Needs e2e tests and UX approval.

2025-03-03 Design review (Jamal Ortega): UX on graceful degradation defined — show 'partial response' card in Console, include 'compatibility_hint' in response metadata for integrators. Design PR: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/responses-compat-v1

2025-03-05 Sophie Caldwell: Merged ledger draft to docs site (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Responses+Compatibility+Ledger. Next: expand CI harness and add synthetic customer regressions for top-3 gap categories.
implementation_notes: Key technical focus: (A) event normalization layer in the gateway that canonicalizes streaming frames into an internal event enum; (B) signature-compat adapter for function call handoff that converts OpenAI-style arguments to our runtime tool API with shallow validation; (C) structured-output sanitizer that preserves top-level keys and includes lossiness metadata when fields are dropped or coerced.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Silent loss of structured fields when converting between schemas -> Mitigation: Add lossiness metadata and opt-in strict-mode for enterprise tenants
Risk: Increased tail-latency when applying runtime conversion hooks -> Mitigation: Benchmark hooks, introduce fast-paths for common event shapes, and fail-open for low-priority routes
Risk: Breaking customer integrations by changing streamed event shapes -> Mitigation: Canary rollout with response-level compatibility header and telemetry to measure errors
test_plan: Unit tests for event normalization layer covering 50+ streaming event permutations
Integration tests that replay recorded OpenAI Responses session logs and verify outputs against ledger expectations
Canary traffic experiment to measure real-world signal for 2 weeks before wide rollout
Dashboard queries to track compatibility_hint frequency, structured-output coercions, and function-call failures
